# pcd_compute_aggregate (Resource)

Manages a Nova host aggregate: a named group of hypervisors with metadata the scheduler can match, and optionally an availability zone. The PCD UI calls these host aggregates; the stretched cluster (failure domain) feature is built from them, as the Failure domains guide shows. Aggregate names are unique across the region and share their namespace with clusters, because PCD's resource manager creates one aggregate per cluster under the cluster's name: an aggregate cannot take a cluster's name, and a `pcd_cluster` created later with an aggregate's name fails. Those per-cluster aggregates, and the aggregate named `compute`, belong to PCD and cannot be managed or imported here. Requires an admin token.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Hypervisors resolved from the hostnames they report.
data "pcd_host" "hyp1" {
  name = "hyp1.example.com"
}

data "pcd_host" "hyp2" {
  name = "hyp2.example.com"
}

# A host aggregate inside cluster-1: zone is the cluster's name, because PCD
# makes each cluster an availability zone named after it, and a host can only
# join aggregates of its own cluster's zone. Scheduler filters that match
# aggregate metadata (against flavor extra specs, for example) can then steer
# instances to these hosts.
resource "pcd_compute_aggregate" "ssd" {
  name  = "ssd-hosts"
  zone  = "cluster-1"
  hosts = [data.pcd_host.hyp1.id, data.pcd_host.hyp2.id]

  metadata = {
    ssd = "true"
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) The aggregate name, unique in the region. Updatable in place.

### Optional

- `hosts` (Set of String) The hypervisors in the aggregate, by resmgr host UUID: `data.pcd_host.<name>.id` or `pcd_host_cluster_role.<name>.host_id` (PCD names a host's compute service after that UUID). Authoritative: hosts added outside Terraform are removed on the next apply. Nova knows a host only once its hypervisor role has converged, so adding one waits up to five minutes for it; when the role is assigned in the same configuration, set `wait_until_converged = true` on it.
- `metadata` (Map of String) Key-value metadata the scheduler's aggregate filters match against. Authoritative: keys set outside Terraform are removed on the next apply, and omitting the attribute removes every key. `availability_zone` (use `zone`) and `pf9-managed` are reserved. Nova's aggregate filters in PCD compare metadata with flavor extra specs, image properties and project IDs, so choose keys that do not collide with those unless you mean them to.
- `region` (String) The region. Defaults to the provider's region. Changing this forces a new resource.
- `zone` (String) The availability zone the aggregate's hosts form. In PCD a cluster is an availability zone named after the cluster, so this should be the hosts' cluster name (`pcd_cluster.<name>.name`) or unset: a host can belong to aggregates of only one zone, so adding a host whose cluster differs fails. Changing the zone from one value to another updates in place, which Nova refuses when the aggregate's hosts already run instances. Nova cannot remove a zone once set, so removing this attribute replaces the aggregate. When importing an aggregate that has a zone, set `zone` to it in the configuration first, or the plan replaces the aggregate.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The Nova aggregate ID, a decimal integer.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax. The IDs are assigned by PCD; the
[Importing guide](https://registry.terraform.io/providers/platform9/pcd/latest/docs/guides/importing)
explains how to look them up.

```shell
# The import ID is the aggregate's integer ID: pcdctl aggregate list
terraform import pcd_compute_aggregate.ssd <id>
```
